feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Stablecoin Runs as Stress Signals for Safe Assets: Episode-Level Evidence for Central Bank Monitoring
entry.summary: Stablecoin Runs as Safe-Asset Stress Signals: Episode-Level Evidence for Central Bank Surveillance arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines whether stablecoin runs contain information about U.S. Treasury yields, using daily data on USDT, USDC and BUSD from 2021 to 2025 across five stress episodes. Flows are measured by changes in token units rather than market capitalisation. During three panic-driven runs, a one-billion-dollar five-day redemption was associated with an 8.5 basis point fall in the three-month bill yield within ten trading days, while two regulatory episodes showed no such signal.

entry.title: Signed but Unbound: The Gap Between What AI Payment Mandates Specify and What Crypto Wallets Enforce
entry.summary: Signed but Unbound: The Authority Gap Between Agent Commerce Mandates and Crypto Wallet Signatures arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper examines the gap between the payment terms an AI agent's commerce protocol specifies, such as merchant, order, amount, and facilitator, and the fields a token contract actually enforces through the wallet signature. The authors define nine constraint classes and derive them for 12 authorization configurations, including Coinbase's deployed Commerce Payments Protocol, with all 31,800 trials on local copies of deployed contract code matching the derivation. They introduce MandateLock, a minimal implementation that rejects all 10,800 modified mandates on deployed token code while accepting signatures from two independent signers. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors define an authority gap between agent payment mandates and wallet signatures, derive nine constraint classes, and report trials on deployed token contract copies plus sampled on-chain rede

entry.title: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Transition
entry.summary: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Transition arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a migration design for Ethereum to post-quantum cryptography. Owners can cheaply enroll post-quantum keys using their existing signatures before ECDSA is scheduled for retirement, and can correct the enrollment with a zero-knowledge proof of their BIP-39 seed until a common deadline. Unenrolled accounts stay frozen and can be recovered by seed proof without a deadline. The authors prove account guarantees, model-check the rules, implement the design in go-ethereum and a Lean consensus client, and report a proof of about 190 KB that verifies in 38 ms. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine correctable enrollment with deadline-free seed proofs for Ethereum's post-quantum migration. They report a go-ethereum implementation and a 190 KB, 38 ms verifying STARK.

entry.title: Signed, Valid, and Unauthorized: Wallet-Side Checks for Agent Stablecoin Payments
entry.summary: Signed, Valid, and Unauthorized: Authority Closure at the Trust Boundary Between Agent Commerce Protocols and Crypto Wallets arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines how wallets signing objects for agent commerce payments in stablecoins can grant transfer permissions beyond what the buyer approved. The authors define authority closure as all transfer sequences a signed object can enable and build Closure, a wallet-side checker covering 13 families of signed objects. In an evaluation of 2,130 generated objects, Closure rejected all objects with an observed violation and accepted the rest. The median decision time was at most 12 microseconds per family. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define authority closure for signed wallet objects, characterize when they respect the mandate, and report a 13-family checker evaluated on generated objects and x402 clients.

entry.title: Release-Bound Withdrawal Authorization (RBWA) for Bitcoin Custody
entry.summary: Release-Bound Withdrawal Authorization for Bitcoin Custody arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper addresses the risk that a compromised cryptocurrency withdrawal backend could request signatures on unauthorized payments. It proposes Release-Bound Withdrawal Authorization (RBWA), which orders permits against pause in a replicated journal and restores exposure when closing evidence disappears from Bitcoin's active chain. In matched synthetic schedules, active probes reduced permits through compromised leases from 20 to 9 out of 33, with one false fence.

entry.title: DispersedBFT: A Byzantine-Fault-Tolerant Consensus Protocol That Removes the Primary Bottleneck
entry.summary: DispersedBFT: Bottleneck-Free Primary-Backup Consensus using Dispersed Replication arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes DispersedBFT, a high-performance consensus protocol similar to PBFT. It uses information dispersal to spread the work of replicating requests from the primary to the backup nodes, removing the primary bottleneck. Several variants are presented, using message authentication codes and Merkle proofs for low CPU cost, or digital signatures for low communication cost. The authors report a throughput of 3.4 million transactions per second with 43 replicas, up to 6.2 times faster than PBFT and 2.6 times faster than HotStuff.

entry.title: ChainIT Transaction Truth: A Zero-Trust Control Architecture for Stablecoin and Web3 Wallet Payments
entry.summary: ChainIT Transaction Truth: Stablecoins, Web3 Wallets, and Multi-Rail Commerce. A Zero-Trust Control Plane for Verified Identity, Organizational Authority, Runtime Compliance, Secure Wallet Execution, and Immutable Settlement Evidence arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes the ChainIT Transaction Truth Architecture, a control system for commercial transactions using stablecoins and Web3 wallets. Before wallet execution, it adds verified identity, organizational authority, transaction-level compliance checks, exact-digest approval, atomic capacity reservation, and a single-use execution credential. After the transaction, it records settlement, reconciliation, and lifecycle evidence. The authors argue that controlling a key is not identity, and that network confirmation is not complete commercial settlement.

entry.title: Cost study of verifying farm sensor data on Ethereum after its 2025 upgrades
entry.summary: Authenticating IoT Data on Ethereum after Pectra and Fusaka: A Cost Study of Signature Schemes, Batching and Anchoring for Agricultural Supply Chain Finance arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how cheaply IoT sensor records from farms can be authenticated and anchored on Ethereum after the Pectra and Fusaka upgrades, to support agricultural supply chain finance. It compares four replay-protected signature designs and measures on-chain gas costs with batching and Merkle anchoring. Batched ECDSA authentication falls to 8,963 gas per record, and secp256k1 ECDSA remains the cheapest option.

entry.title: Double Entropy Fit Index (DEFI): An information-theoretic method for dimensionality reduction and clustering
entry.summary: The Double Entropy Fit Index (DEFI): An Information-Theoretic Approach to Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces the Double-Entropy Fit Index (DEFI), a regularized information-theoretic criterion for choosing among candidate graph partitions and reduced representations. It combines entropy-based compression with relevance preservation and penalizes model dimensionality, cluster imbalance, and partition fragmentation. On a 243-condition factor recovery benchmark, DEFI achieved an overall exact recovery rate of 97.2%, and across ten clustering benchmarks, DEFI-guided Gaussian mixtures reached a mean ARI of 0.929.

entry.title: Vehicle-to-vehicle communication using blockchain, federated learning and 6G
entry.summary: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes a vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication approach combining blockchain, federated learning, and latency and resource allocation optimization. It is evaluated using packet delivery ratio, model accuracy, and latency, and is reported to outperform existing techniques. The system adds security through consensus optimization and k-anonymity for data privacy. The authors claim higher reliability, lower latency, and better resource utilization than traditional 5G.

entry.title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Testing Attack Detection on Solana
entry.summary: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper builds a lock-and-mint cross-chain bridge in Rust on a local Solana validator, with four exploitable variants, two reproducing flaws from the Cashio and Wormhole incidents and two based on vulnerability classes in Solana security audits. Five open-weight language models in six configurations were tested on source code with and without comments, and their 16,800 responses were graded by two blinded LLM graders. Without comments, models correctly diagnosed 24% of vulnerable source inputs while often flagging the secure bridge; original comments raised source diagnosis to 60%.

entry.title: Twisted Towers: A Faster, Fully Costed SexTNFS Attack on BLS12-381
entry.summary: Twisted Towers: Fully Costed Special Tower NFS Attacks on BLS12-381 and BN254 IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies a special exTNFS attack on discrete logarithms in the target group of BLS12-381. It presents a (6,2) design whose every step, from relation collection to individual logarithms, is priced in one instruction-level model. The design uses an explicit twisted tower so that relations and ideals come in orbits of four. The authors also note that yield estimates over TNFS coefficient cubes overcount unit multiples. All estimates rest on stated heuristics, nothing was run at full size, and BLS12-381's practical security is unchanged. Correction Nov 18, 2026: Moved from "Cryptography & Security" to "Crypto & Blockchain"

entry.title: Incentive Alignment for Electricity Data Assets in China: A Blockchain-Based Contribution-Credit Framework
entry.summary: Incentive Alignment for Electricity Data Assets in China: A Blockchain-Enabled Contribution-Credit Framework arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes a blockchain-based contribution-credit framework that encourages truthful reporting of operational contributions when supporting evidence arrives late. It links authenticated evidence to contribution recognition through dynamic credit updating, escrow, report-linked penalties, and automated incentive execution. The Chinese electricity market is the primary setting, with two representative coordination scenarios and adaptations for UK and US market structures. Simulation, security analysis, and blockchain implementation experiments assess its behavioural effects and feasibility.

entry.title: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Protecting Power Systems Against Cyber-Physical Threats
entry.summary: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Cyber-Physical Resilience in Electrical Power and Energy Systems arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes RESILAGENT, a conceptual architecture for electrical power and energy systems facing combined cyber intrusions, physical sabotage, and climate-driven stress. It is built on three pillars (sensing and data intelligence, resilience analytics and reporting, and incident response and recovery), coordinated by a cloud-based orchestrator and a Detect-Simulate-Decide-Sign loop. The framework integrates agentic AI, multimodal large language models, real-time digital twins, and a permissioned blockchain, and is evaluated on two operator scenarios and an IEEE-bus micro-benchmark.

entry.title: Optimal Dynamic Fees for L2s: A Vault-Based Approach
entry.summary: Optimal Dynamic Fees for L2s: A Vault Approach arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper models the cost of Layer 2 blockchains posting data to Layer 1 as a vault, where user fees add to its balance and posting costs subtract from it, so surpluses and deficits build up over time. The authors treat the vault as a discrete-time control system and derive in closed form the optimal trade-off between vault tracking and fee smoothness in an idealized benchmark. The optimal rule keeps a fraction of the previous fee and corrects in proportion to the current vault error, with this fraction being the single parameter that traces the whole trade-off frontier.

entry.title: Physical "baryonic keys" for inheriting crypto-assets, and an improved TFCP protocol
entry.summary: Baryonic Keys and the Inheritance of Crypto-Assets: Revisiting the Tales From the Crypt Protocol arXiv · Nov 16, 2026Crypto-asset inheritance is hard because ownership equals knowledge of a private key, which is lost if its owner dies without sharing it. The paper revisits the Tales From the Crypt Protocol (TFCP), which handles blockchain-based acknowledgment of death, and introduces a "baryonic key": a physical object whose bits are obtained only by measurement, never stored digitally, and existing in exactly n copies. It proposes TFCP-B, which requires both a secret shared among registrars and a baryonic key's response to decrypt a will, and notes remaining limitations such as shallow-account attacks.

entry.title: Type-Confusion Security: Keeping Attackers Who Ignore Types from Fooling Trusted Code
entry.summary: Type-Confusion Security arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper defines type confusion security, the property that attackers who do not follow the type system have no more power than attackers who fully obey it. It formalizes this as a real-ideal emulation and, in an information-flow-typed core calculus, proves that run-time checks enforce security against ill-typed attackers. The proof is mechanized in Lean. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formally define type confusion security via real-ideal emulation and prove run-time checks enforce it, mechanized in Lean.

entry.title: AllocFlow: Generating Portfolio Trades Directly from Raw Market Data
entry.summary: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper introduces AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that generates joint allocations across multiple assets directly from raw market histories, rather than separating forecasting from portfolio construction. It trains in two stages: imitation of a teacher strategy to shape candidate portfolios, then group-relative reinforcement learning using portfolio-level financial rewards. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, reinforcement learning raised annualized net return from 27.79% to 51.38% and Calmar ratio from 0.955 to 4.043, and the model reached a Calmar ratio of 4.90 on six months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.

entry.title: iGRAIL: Blockchain-based generative federated learning for trustworthy healthcare AI
entry.summary: iGRAIL: Blockchain-Based Generative Federated Learning for Trustworthy Healthcare Intelligence arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper proposes iGRAIL, a framework that combines blockchain, generative local learning, and differential privacy so that healthcare institutions can train models together without sharing raw patient records. Cryptographic communication, blockchain verification, and smart-contract access control ensure that only authorized, authentic, fresh, and intact model updates are used for federated aggregation. Tested on four healthcare datasets, iGRAIL improved accuracy, F1-score, and MCC over conventional federated learning and blockchain-based federated learning on two large diabetes datasets, while reducing the privacy-loss parameter, at the cost of added computational overhead.

entry.title: Efficient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges: Hash-based proof verification on Bitcoin
entry.summary: Toward Eﬃcient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses BitVM-style protocols, which verify succinct proofs on Bitcoin by garbling a proof verifier off-chain. It proposes a post-quantum alternative using a hash-based STARK verifier fed with hash-based one-time keys, avoiding number-theoretic assumptions. The authors compile a complete verifier for WHIR-based STARK proofs from Ziren into a Boolean circuit and report circuit costs for the final recursive WHIR-proof verifier. They also measure the total virtual size of the transactions publishing the input with translated Winternitz keys, reporting 4.26 million virtual bytes for one key set.
